Reforming voting qualifications is one of the first steps to fixing this shithole government. Only people who are competent and have a stake in the government running well should have a say in how it runs. In my ideal world, in order to vote, you must meet these qualifications:

1) You must be a citizen of the country (duh, but I guess it needs to be said these days). Dual-citizenship should not be a thing. There is no reason to assume that people with loyalty and membership to other nations would always hold this nation's interests first.

2) You must not have received more in direct public benefits than you paid in taxes during the previous election cycle. People who take from the taxpayers by force of government have no incentive to make sure the government runs efficiently and doesn't take more than is needed from taxpayers. Plus, if politicians can get elected and do whatever they want as long as they give enough of other people's money away, you're going to get insane corruption and insurmountable debt.

3) You should be required to pass some sort of IQ test or critical thinking skills test, and rank average or above. You wouldn't want a retard doing the hiring for your business - no matter their opinions or worldview - for the same reason you wouldn't want retards hiring your politicians.

4) Immigrants should be required to have a probationary period of a certain number of years before they can vote, if they're allowed a vote at all. If I showed up to Japan just last month and am now voting in their elections, I am probably going to vote in line with the cultural values gained from a life in America. You don't get to vote for your new country to become the homeland you just left.

5) People who've given some defined category of service to the country (military folks come to mind) should have an easier time qualifying for the vote. If you are willing to give your blood and sweat (and potentially your life) in the service of our nation, it seems very likely that you'd try to vote in the nation's best interests.

6) If people under a certain age are not mature enough to responsibly use the full legal rights of an adult citizen (drinking alcohol, military service, etc.), then they are certainly not mature enough to decide how the government should be run. If your demographic generally can't make good long-term decisions in their personal lives without the supervision of Mom and Dad, then they have no place in deciding foreign policy or economic regulations for hundreds of millions of people.

If you start instituting sensible voting requirements like these, you will see a drastically more successful country by next election.
